summary: Send back: see what to send.

findings.title: Couldn't confirm: VOC (air quality)
findings.detail: VOC lower than SCAQMD 1168 requires (250 g/L: the Rule 1168 architectural sealant limit; the number comes from the rule, not the spec).
findings.why_it_matters: Without confirmed low VOC levels, we can’t be sure the sealant meets air quality rules that protect workers and occupants.

findings.title: Couldn't confirm: astm g21 rating
findings.detail: Firestopping materials shall have mold and mildew resistance rating of zero(0) in accordance with ASTM G21.
findings.why_it_matters: Mold resistance is critical in damp areas—without proof of zero growth per ASTM G21, we risk long-term performance issues.

findings.title: Couldn't confirm: Temperature rating (T)
findings.detail: Both quoted ratings are needed for this comparison.
findings.why_it_matters: Temperature ratings tell us if the sealant will hold up during a fire; we need both values to verify it matches the required fire-resistance rating.

findings.title: Test standards
findings.detail: Package states ASTM E 814, UL 1479, ASTM E 1966, UL 2079; allowed: astm e814, astm e119, ul 1479.

highlights.quote:
Meets the criteria of ASTM E 814  (UL 1479) standard test method for fire tests of through-penetration fire stops tested
under positive pressure, and ASTM E 1966 (UL 2079) standard test for fire-resistive joint systems.

findings.title: Data sheet is out of date
findings.detail: The submitted sheet (undated) differs from the current source (January / 2026) on: Pipe types covered, Highest service temperature.
findings.why_it_matters: An outdated data sheet might not reflect current product capabilities—we need the latest version to confirm it covers the right pipe types and temperatures used on site.
